audits.title: 766 Audit of Stratified Treatment Escalation Plan Completion and DNACPR in Patients with Femoral Fractures – 4th Cycle
audits.standard: Internal standard of 100% for STEP form completion, completion within 24 hours, and documented escalation discussion
audits.setting: Fragility fracture ward, South Tees University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: STEP form completion 100% (13% with minor errors); completed within 24 hours 77%; discussion documented for less than full escalation 58% (cognitively intact) and 64% (cognitively impaired).

audits.intervention: Planned: posters, audit in junior doctor induction, email reminders; e-documentation under consideration.
audits.other_findings: This is the 4th cycle; completion within 24 hours improved from cycle 3 but cycle 3 figures are not given.
audits.citation: Masala I, Rashinkar S, Bairstow D, Manjunath P. 766 Audit of Stratified Treatment Escalation Plan Completion and DNACPR in Patients with Femoral Fractures – 4th Cycle. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.265.

audits.title: Improving Completion Rates of Treatment Escalation Plan (TEP) in a London Teaching Hospital: A Quality Improvement Study.
audits.standard: Trust treatment escalation plan (TEP) policy: TEP completed for emergency adult admissions, within 48 hours
audits.setting: Orthopaedic wards, University Hospital Lewisham (London teaching hospital), adult inpatients

cycle1.result: Overall TEP completion 69.5%; completed within 48 hours 47.82%; mean time to complete 4.4 days; mean overrides 3.2; longest 35 days; 24 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 30.4% (n=7).

audits.intervention: Revised local TEP pathway/algorithm allowing F1+ doctors to complete TEPs for young patients with simple fractures, algorithm displayed in trauma room, emails, individual teaching, and reminders to discuss TEP status on the post-take ward round.

cycle2.result: Overall completion 88.2%; completed within 48 hours 35.29%; mean time 3.7 days; mean overrides 1.3; longest 13 days; 5 instances of skipping. Incomplete TEPs 11.76% (n=2).

audits.other_findings: Completion within 48 hours fell between cycles despite better overall completion. A junior doctor questionnaire found TEPs were skipped because of competing clinical priorities.
audits.citation: Pattnaik S, Zarifian A, Sidhu GAS, Punwar S. Improving Completion Rates of Treatment Escalation Plan (TEP) in a London Teaching Hospital: A Quality Improvement Study. Cureus. 2023;15(11):e49434. doi:10.7759/cureus.49434. PMID: 38149128.

audits.title: 123 Quality Improvement Project on Completion of Respect Form in the Community At Jean Bishop Integrated Care Centre (ICC)
audits.standard: Published ReSPECT data (NHS Forth Valley report: 39% completion, 79% uploaded)
audits.setting: Jean Bishop Integrated Care Centre, Hull (community)

cycle1.result: Of 71 without a form, 57 had discussions (80%) and 29 forms were completed (41%); 24/29 (82%) uploaded.

audits.intervention: Posters of results in clinic rooms and feedback to key team members

cycle2.result: 13 (94%) had ReSPECT discussions and 6 forms completed; 81% had a form or discussion.

audits.other_findings: Regular training and spot checks recommended for sustainability.

audits.title: 3463 Audit of quality of ReSPECT forms in Southmead Hospital
audits.standard: Resuscitation Council UK ReSPECT guidance (17 criteria); target 100% in all criteria
audits.setting: Inpatient medical and surgical wards (excluding acute medical and surgical wards), Southmead Hospital, North Bristol NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Best: CPR recommendation signature and demographics 99.3% (293); worst: mental capacity assessment in notes 15.2% (11/72) and reasoning for lack of capacity 48.6% (35/72); values and fears documented 22%

audits.other_findings: Medical wards performed significantly better than surgical wards on reasoning for lack of capacity (p < 0.05); legal proxy documentation was very low on all wards. Education and a re-audit in 6–12 months were planned.
audits.citation: Sreenivas G, Grange R. 3463 Audit of quality of ReSPECT forms in Southmead Hospital. Age and Ageing. 2026;55(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.059.

audits.title: FTP6.1 A little respect! A closed-loop audit increasing awareness of ReSPECT forms in a busy general surgical department
audits.standard: ReSPECT forms (Resuscitation Council UK) completed for surgical inpatients
audits.setting: General surgical ward, Gloucestershire Royal Hospital (general hospital)

cycle1.result: Completion rate of accurate ReSPECT forms 31%.

audits.intervention: Cycle 1 intervention: a ReSPECT column added to the surgical take list. Cycle 2 intervention: team education with a novel prioritisation poster and a teaching session.

cycle2.result: After the poster and teaching, ReSPECT column use rose to 39% and overall completion was 33%.

audits.other_findings: After the take-list column alone, the column was completed for 15% of inpatients and overall completion was 35%.
audits.citation: Bruno P, McKinlay A, Eva C, Roe T. FTP6.1 A little respect! A closed-loop audit increasing awareness of ReSPECT forms in a busy general surgical department. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.386.

audits.setting: West Middlesex University Hospital, district general hospital; emergency surgical admissions

cycle1.result: 19 (15%) had TEP forms; 5 (26%) by parent surgical team; median time to completion 2 days; 39 of 47 operated patients (83%) had no TEP.

audits.setting: General surgery department, central London hospital; emergency admissions

audits.title: TPTh 8.13 Escalation Planning in Acute General Surgery: Persistent Gaps Highlighted in a 300-Patient Audit
audits.standard: Local trust standard (with Resuscitation Council UK guidance): TEP and DNACPR documented within 24 hours of admission
audits.setting: James Cook University Hospital, unplanned general surgical admissions

cycle1.result: Ceiling-of-care decisions documented in 18% (n=54); only 6% (n=18) had TEP or DNACPR documented within 24 hours; DNACPR present in 12% (n=36), 40% of which lacked clear clerking documentation.

audits.intervention: Planned: structured training for junior doctors and strengthened admission proformas, then re-audit.
audits.other_findings: 68% had CCI ≥4; among hospital DNACPR orders only half were timely.
audits.citation: Arifuzaman M. TPTh 8.13 Escalation Planning in Acute General Surgery: Persistent Gaps Highlighted in a 300-Patient Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.514.

audits.title: Improving the Use of Treatment Escalation Plans in Geriatric Medicine: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: National guidance on treatment escalation plans (no target stated)
audits.setting: Geriatric medicine wards, Glasgow Royal Infirmary (tertiary hospital)

cycle1.result: TEP completed in 21 of 75 (28%); median time to TEP 10.5 days (IQR 7-14); DNACPR documentation 55%; consultant involvement 12%.

audits.intervention: Paper-based admission checklist, then a multidisciplinary teaching programme.

cycle2.result: TEP completed in 72 of 125 (58%); median time 5 days (IQR 3-8); DNACPR documentation 73%; consultant involvement 27%.

audits.other_findings: After the checklist alone (cycle 1, n=75) TEP completion was 32 of 75 (43%). Consultant involvement was linked to earlier completion (median 4 vs 7 days, P = 0.03).
audits.citation: Choo JH, Dee R, McElroy M. Improving the Use of Treatment Escalation Plans in Geriatric Medicine: A Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2025;17(10):e95283. doi:10.7759/cureus.95283. PMID: 41287712.

audits.title: TO ESCALATE OR TO PALLIATE? AN AUDIT OF PATIENTS AT RISK OF DETERIORATION ON MEDICAL WARDS
audits.standard: Modified tool based on NICE CG50: doctor/outreach contacted and patient reviewed after EWS >5 (100%)
audits.setting: Medical wards, Airedale General Hospital; district general hospital

cycle1.result: Doctor or outreach contacted in 70% with EWS >5; a third not reviewed; only 5 of 30 had a clear escalation plan.

audits.intervention: Results presented and published in hospital newsletter; escalation plan form and sticker being piloted.
audits.other_findings: Some patients with palliative conditions had no DNACPR consideration.
audits.citation: Grewal B, Johnson F. TO ESCALATE OR TO PALLIATE? AN AUDIT OF PATIENTS AT RISK OF DETERIORATION ON MEDICAL WARDS. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2014;4(Suppl 1):A81.2-A81. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2014-000654.231.
